Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

pedkindraw 0.0.1 (development version)

The first version, not yet on CRAN. Most of its code is a copy of nprcgenekeepr’s at nprcgenekeepr’s commit baef1e12c; the items marked “New” were written for pedkindraw. Where the copy now differs from nprcgenekeepr’s code, DIVERGENCE.md in the repository says how and why.

Drawing

  • makePedigreeMatingLayout() lays out a pedigree’s animals and matings, and drawPedigreeDiagram() draws the layout as an interactive visNetwork graph: a symbol for each sex, a slash through each animal that has died, up to four conditions, twin lines, matings between relatives marked, an animal drawn twice where the layout needs it with its two places joined by a dashed line, a legend, a “Select by id” box and a PNG export button. makePedigreeDiagramData() makes a simpler drawing’s nodes and edges.
  • New: with two or more conditions, each condition’s row in drawPedigreeDiagram()‘s legend shows a circle cut into the same sections as the animals’ symbols, with that condition’s section filled, so the legend says which section is which. nprcgenekeepr’s legend still shows a filled hexagon for each condition.
  • New: the “Select by id” box lists the animals only; nprcgenekeepr’s also lists the routing points (ids starting __jog_) a drawing adds to step a line around an animal: 196 of the 571 entries in the drawing vignette’s colony drawing.
  • New: makePedigreeMatingLayout() stops on an animal id that starts with __jog_, as for the other prefixes it keeps for its own nodes; nprcgenekeepr accepts one, and its drawing can then have two nodes with that id.
  • New: makePedigreeMatingLayout() and makePedigreeDiagramData() stop when a condition column (affected, affected2, …) holds a number other than 0 and 1, naming the column and the numbers. A measured trait (2.5, 0.3, 9) was drawn affected wherever it was not 0, with no message, as it still is in nprcgenekeepr. TRUE, FALSE, NA, 0 and 1 (kinship2’s codes, which asPedFrame() writes) and text read as before.
  • New: an animal whose affected status is unknown (NA) is filled grey (#BEBEBE, R’s “grey”, as Pedixplorer fills it), with one condition, or has that condition’s section grey, with two to four, so it no longer looks unaffected; makePedigreeDiagramData() fills it grey too. The legend then has a grey row “Affected status unknown” after the condition rows, and the drawing is 45 px taller for it. nprcgenekeepr still fills an unknown status white. Text in a condition column that as.logical() cannot read (such as “yes”, or “1” read as text) is unknown, so it is now drawn grey.
  • New: makePedigreeMatingLayout() and makePedigreeDiagramData() take maxNameChars, the most characters of the name column written under an animal’s id, 15 by default as before: a longer name is cut and ends in “…”, and the hover text keeps it whole. A line break counts as one character. maxNameChars = Inf writes every name whole, as kinship2 and Pedixplorer write their labels; a long name can then run into the labels of the animals beside it. nprcgenekeepr cuts every name after 15 characters.
  • New: makePedigreeMatingLayout() and makePedigreeDiagramData() take conditionColors, the colours of the affected conditions, by default the four drawn before (pink, orange, sky blue and bluish green). Each is a name R knows, such as “orange”, or a code, such as “#E69F00”, and is written as its “#RRGGBB” code, the colour R means by it: a browser reads most of R’s colour names as no colour, and “grey” as a darker grey. The layout fills the symbols with them and keeps them in its conditions table, from which drawPedigreeDiagram() now paints the sections and the legend, so all three agree; before, colours edited in that table reached the legend but not the sections. A colour R does not know, a number, a transparent colour, white, the grey of an unknown status, a colour given twice, or fewer colours than conditions drawn stops, with a message naming them. nprcgenekeepr’s colours are fixed.
  • New: makePedigreeMatingLayout() and makePedigreeDiagramData() take conditionThresholds, cut-offs for measured traits. A condition column of numbers is drawn by its cut-off, a comparison and a number, such as conditionThresholds = c(affected_glucose = ">= 126", affected_hb = "< 13"): an animal whose number passes is affected, one whose number does not is unaffected, and one with no number is unknown (grey). The rule goes into the condition’s name, so the legend reads “Affected (glucose ≥ 126)” and the hover text “Affected (glucose ≥ 126): Yes (140)”. > and < decide as Pedixplorer’s threshold does. Without a cut-off a number other than 0 and 1 still stops, and the message now names conditionThresholds. nprcgenekeepr has no cut-off.
  • New: makePedigreeMatingLayout() reads a column genotyped (TRUE, FALSE, NA, 1, 0, or text such as “TRUE”): each genotyped animal’s symbol is drawn with its outline 4 pixels wide, where every other symbol’s is 1, and its hover text says “Genotyped: Yes”, “No” or “Unknown”; any other value stops, naming the column. drawPedigreeDiagram()’s legend then has a row “Genotyped”, a square with the thick outline, and the drawing is 45 px taller. Pedixplorer marks an available animal with a green border; nprcgenekeepr has no such mark. Without the column every drawing is as before.
  • New: makePedigreeMatingLayout() reads a column carrier (TRUE, FALSE, NA, 1, 0, or text such as “TRUE”), for animals that have the genetic trait but are not expected to show the disease: each carrier’s symbol is drawn with a black dot at its centre, on top of its fill, its sections and the deceased slash, and its hover text says “Carrier: Yes”, “No” or “Unknown”; any other value stops, naming the column. drawPedigreeDiagram()’s legend then has a row “Carrier”, a circle with the dot, and the drawing is 45 px taller. A Pedixplorer object converted by asPedFrame() keeps its carriers in that column. Pedixplorer draws a smaller dot; nprcgenekeepr has no such mark. Without the column every drawing is as before.
  • New: makePedigreeMatingLayout() reads the columns proband and consultand (TRUE, FALSE, NA, 1, 0, or text such as “TRUE”): the proband, an affected animal through whom the family came to attention, and the consultand, an animal for whom counselling or testing is sought. Each is drawn with a black arrow pointing at its symbol from the lower left, a proband’s with “P” beside its tail, and the hover text says “Proband:” and “Consultand:” “Yes”, “No” or “Unknown”; any other value stops, naming the column, and so does an animal marked both, naming it. drawPedigreeDiagram()’s legend then has a row “Proband” and a row “Consultand”, each the arrow, and the drawing is 45 px taller for each; the view takes in each arrow, so one at the left edge is not cut off. An id starting __mark_ is now refused, as the other reserved prefixes are. A Pedixplorer object converted by asPedFrame() keeps both columns. Pedixplorer draws a smaller arrow at 45 degrees, reads NA as FALSE and warns of a proband who is not affected, which pedkindraw does not check; nprcgenekeepr has no such mark. Without the columns every drawing is as before.
  • New: makePedigreeMatingLayout() reads a column evaluated (TRUE, FALSE, NA, 1, 0, or text such as “TRUE”), for animals with a documented evaluation: each is drawn with a black “*” to the right of the upper-right corner of its symbol, clear of the deceased slash and the lines, and its hover text says “Evaluated: Yes”, “No” or “Unknown”; any other value stops, naming the column. drawPedigreeDiagram()’s legend then has a row “Evaluated”, the “*”, and the drawing is 45 px taller; the view takes in each “*”, so one at the right edge is not cut off. An id starting __eval_ is now refused, as the other reserved prefixes are. A Pedixplorer object converted by asPedFrame() keeps the column. Pedixplorer draws its “*” just outside the corner, where it meets a deceased animal’s slash, reads NA as FALSE and has no legend row; nprcgenekeepr has no such mark. Without the column every drawing is as before.
  • New: makePedigreeMatingLayout() reads a column fertility in Pedixplorer’s words and values: “infertile” (also “steril”, FALSE or 0), “infertile_choice_na” for an animal with no offspring by choice or for an unknown reason (also “infertile_choice” or “infertile_na”), and “fertile” (also TRUE or 1), in any case, NA where it is not recorded. An infertile animal is drawn with a black line down from its symbol and two bars, as in Pedixplorer, and one with no offspring by choice or for an unknown reason with a line and one bar; the animal’s id moves down below the bars. Its hover text says “Fertility: Fertile”, “Infertile”, “No offspring by choice or for an unknown reason” or “Unknown”; any other value stops, naming the column (Pedixplorer reads such a value as fertile). An animal with offspring is marked as recorded, since a colony animal can be sterilised after it has bred (Pedixplorer refuses it). drawPedigreeDiagram()’s legend then has a row “Infertile” and a row “No offspring”, each its mark, 45 px each; the view takes in each moved id, so one at the bottom edge is not cut off. An id starting __fert_ is now refused, as the other reserved prefixes are. A Pedixplorer object converted by asPedFrame() keeps the column and is drawn with its marks. nprcgenekeepr has no such mark. Without the column every drawing is as before.
  • New: makePedigreeMatingLayout() reads a column miscarriage in Pedixplorer’s words and values: “SAB” for a spontaneous abortion (also “spontaneous” or “spontaneous abortion”), “TOP” for a termination of pregnancy (also “termination”, “terminated” or “termination of pregnancy”), “ECT” for an ectopic pregnancy (also “ectopic” or “ectopic pregnancy”), and FALSE, 0 or “no” for none, without spaces and in any case, NA where it is not recorded. A miscarriage is drawn as a triangle in place of its symbol, as in Pedixplorer, but 0.6 the size, so it is not the “Unknown” sex’s triangle; a termination’s or an ectopic pregnancy’s has a black line across it and an ectopic pregnancy’s “ECT” under it, as in Pedixplorer. Its id moves down into the row of the other ids, and it has no deceased slash, which would lie along a termination’s line. Its hover text says “Miscarriage: Spontaneous abortion (SAB)”, “Termination of pregnancy (TOP)”, “Ectopic pregnancy (ECT)”, “No” or “Unknown”; any other value stops, naming the column (Pedixplorer reads such a value as none, TRUE and 1 among them). A miscarriage that is a sire or dam, or that the fertility column marks infertile or with no offspring, stops, naming it, as Pedixplorer refuses both. drawPedigreeDiagram()’s legend then has a row “Miscarriage”, “Termination” and “Ectopic” for each kind drawn, its triangle, 45 px each; the view keeps the room a full-size symbol would have, so a long id at the edge is not cut off. An id starting __misc_ is now refused, as the other reserved prefixes are. A Pedixplorer object converted by asPedFrame() keeps the column and is drawn with its marks. nprcgenekeepr has no such mark. Without the column every drawing is as before.
  • New: makePedigreeMatingLayout(symbolSize = ) sets the size of the animals’ symbols as a multiple of the size drawn before (1, the default), as kinship2’s and Pedixplorer’s symbolsize does: each animal and each repeat appearance is drawn 25 times it units across, rounded to a whole unit, and the mating points keep theirs. The layout works out its lines’ detours around the symbols from it, and an infertile animal’s and a miscarriage’s id moves down in proportion. Since the drawing zooms to fit, a larger symbol leaves less room between the symbols: measured at 500 px, from 2 the symbols reach the lines and the mating points, and at 3 the rectilinear layout warns that it could not clear every symbol. With symbols smaller than full size, drawPedigreeDiagram() keeps the room a full-size symbol would have, so a long id at the edge is not cut off. An id starting __size_ is now refused, as the other reserved prefixes are. Anything but one positive number stops. nprcgenekeepr has no such argument. At 1 every layout and drawing is as before.
  • New: makePedigreeMatingLayout(textSize = ) sets the size of the animals’ ids and names as a multiple of the 14 px written before (1, the default), as kinship2’s and Pedixplorer’s cex does: every node gets 14 times it as its font.size, rounded to a whole pixel. The marks’ own words (a proband’s “P”, an ectopic pregnancy’s “ECT”), the twins’ labels and the symbols keep their sizes, and the layout’s places and lines are the same at every text size. With text larger than before, drawPedigreeDiagram() keeps room for the outermost labels, so a long id at the edge is not cut off (measured at 500 px: without that room the 10-character ids at the edges lost 8-10 px at 1.4 and 27-29 px at 2), and an infertile animal’s and a miscarriage’s moved id keeps its room below its mark. Since the drawing zooms to fit, larger text leaves less room between the ids: an id of 10 characters is 118 units wide at 1.4 and 165 at 2, and the animals in a row are 120 apart. An id starting __text_ is now refused, as the other reserved prefixes are. Anything but one positive number stops. nprcgenekeepr has no such argument. At 1 every layout and drawing is as before.
  • New: makePedigreeMatingLayout(columnSpacing = , rowSpacing = ) set the distance between neighbouring animals in a row and between generations as multiples of the 120 and 150 units used before (1, the defaults), each rounded to a whole unit, so a drawing can be made wider or deeper, as kinship2’s distances follow the width and height of its page. Every place in the layout is the one before times the spacing, and the rectilinear lines’ steps and curves are worked out at the spacing given. Since the drawing zooms to fit, wider spacing leaves the symbols and text smaller beside the distances. Larger text needs wider columns: at textSize = 2 an id of 10 characters is up to 167 units wide, so neighbours’ ids run together at columnSpacing = 1 and stand apart at 1.4. Measured at 500 px, columns at 0.5 lay long ids over their neighbours’ and rows at 0.5 run the lines from parents to their offspring through the parents’ ids. Anything but one positive number stops. nprcgenekeepr has no such arguments. At 1 every layout and drawing is as before.
  • New: makePedigreeMatingLayout(lineWidth = ) sets the width of the lines as a multiple of the widths drawn before (1, the default), as kinship2’s and Pedixplorer’s lwd does. Every line between animals, the mating line of related parents (4 times it), each symbol’s outline and the lines of each mark (the deceased slash, the proband’s arrow, the evaluated star, the infertile bars, the miscarriage line and the lines between a symbol’s sections) follow it, and the dashed lines’ dashes and gaps grow with it, so a thick line stays dashed (kept at their old length, the DZ twins’ line would be solid at 5, like the MZ twins’). A genotyped animal’s outline is the line width plus 3 (4 at 1, as before), so its fill keeps more of the symbol than 4 times the width would leave. The legend keeps its widths. The width is not rounded, and the drawing’s zoom is the same at every width, so thicker lines leave less room: measured at 500 px, at 3 the lines and outlines reach the ids in 4 of 16 drawings (2 at 1). Anything but one positive number stops. nprcgenekeepr has no such argument. At 1 every layout and drawing is as before.
  • New: makePedigreeMatingLayout(matings = ) draws two animals as mates although they have no offspring together, as kinship2’s relation code 4 and Pedixplorer’s “Spouse” rows do: a data frame with the columns sire and dam, one row per mating (other columns are ignored, so getMatings()’s result can be passed with rows added). The two are drawn side by side on one row, joined at a mating point with no line down, whose hover reads “0 offspring”; before, both were left out of the drawing when neither had parents or offspring (isolatedIds). An animal with other matings is drawn at each, as for two matings with offspring. A mate hint may place such a mating. A row naming an animal not in ped (as after trimming) is left out with a message; a pair named twice, in either column, is drawn once; any sexes are drawn as given. Anything but NULL or a data frame with those columns stops, as do NA and the same id as sire and dam. nprcgenekeepr has no such argument. Without it every layout is as before.
  • New: the legend’s four lines (the dashed line joining two places of the same animal, and the three twin lines) have no arrowheads, as the drawing’s own lines have none, and each line’s label sits on white. nprcgenekeepr’s legend draws an arrowhead at the right end of each line, which covers the end of “Same animal, again” in drawings 776 px wide (the package’s website) and 700 px wide.
  • New: layout hints, makePedigreeMatingLayout(hints = ): the left-to-right order of animals and, with mate, the side of a mating each mate is drawn on, in the form kinship2 and Pedixplorer give their hints.
  • New: makePedigreeMatingLayout() returns the hints it used as hints, in the form its hints argument takes, so that makePedigreeMatingLayout(ped, hints = layout$hints) gives the same layout and an edit can start from the layout’s own: order numbers each animal with a parent by the row the layout drew it from (a founder only where your order named it); mate holds your rows, then the layout’s own row for each other mating (none for an animal with three or more matings, where a row can move its mates).
  • New: savePedigreeDiagram(diagram, file, width, height, dpi) writes the widget drawPedigreeDiagram() returns as an SVG, a PDF or a PNG file (the file’s ending chooses), from a script: before, a drawing could be saved only as a web page, or by clicking its “Export Diagram (PNG)” button in a browser. A headless Chrome (the chromote package and Chrome or Chromium on the computer) runs the same drawing the widget shows and a recording layer writes it, so every mark, colour and legend row comes out as drawn, the legend’s pictures as vector pictures, and every id as text a reader can select and zoom to: the widget draws an id only when it would be 4 pixels tall, so its 375 rhesus animals show none until zoomed in, and the file has all 545 id labels (375 distinct, the rest repeat appearances). width and height are the page in inches; left out, the widget’s own size, 10 inches wide. The PDF is that drawing on one page of that size, still vector with its ids as text; each dashed line is written as a row of short strokes, because Chrome would otherwise write every dash as an outline (the 375 animals on a 14 by 7 inch page: 1.0 MB, 5.8 MB without). The PNG is the page at dpi pixels per inch, 300 unless told (a 7 by 5 inch page is 2100 by 1500 pixels). Measured against the live widget in Chrome 157 on macOS, over the pixels that are not white in either, for the SVG and for the PNG at 96 dpi: on the four animals none of the drawing’s and 0.03% of the legend’s differ by more than 100 in a colour channel, on an 18-animal pedigree with all seven marks 0.26% and 0.07%. It stops, saying what is missing, without chromote (in Suggests) or Chrome. It ends every process of the Chrome it starts, on Windows too, where the renderer of a page that never finishes drawing outlives its browser’s close. nprcgenekeepr has no such function.
  • New: the 375 rhesus animals of the example pedigree, with their 3 twin pairs, are one page of savePedigreeDiagram()’s SVG or PDF on a 14 by 7 inch page or on letter paper (8.5 by 11 inches), with every id written: 545 id labels, 375 distinct, and none overlapping another id or label (checked in Chrome on the SVG and with pdftotext on the PDF). The ids are small, under 1 point high on those pages, so a reader zooms in on the SVG or PDF; in a PNG at the default 300 dpi an id is about 3 pixels high (a larger dpi makes it bigger). The drawing vignette’s “Saving a drawing” and “A colony-size drawing” show the files.
  • New: runPedigreeApp(ped, port, launch.browser) starts an app in the web browser that draws a pedigree from a CSV or text file, with no code, for someone who keeps a pedigree in a spreadsheet. It opens the file, the 375 rhesus animals of the sample pedigree, or a ped data frame from R; recognises the id, sire, dam and sex columns by pedkindraw’s names and common others (ego, egoid, indid; father, fatherid, dadid; mother, motherid, momid; gender), in any case and with or without spaces, dots or underscores, and lets you choose each; reads the sex codes m, f, h and u, male, female, hermaphrodite and unknown, and 1 and 2 (male and female, as kinship2 and PLINK files code them) as M, F, H and U, and says so; adds gen; and draws everyone. What the layout says (a warning, an animal it leaves out) is shown on the page, and a pedigree that cannot be drawn is said so. The Checks tab lists checkPedigree()’s problems and the Animals tab the animals read. It needs the shiny package (in Suggests). Pedixplorer’s ped_shiny() is such an app; nprcgenekeepr’s app is its whole colony application, runGeneKeepR().
  • New: runPedigreeApp()‘s app chooses the animals it draws: everyone, one family (the families of two or more animals listed largest first, with their sizes), focal animals with their ancestors and descendants, or focal animals’ near relatives (3 by default, as Pedixplorer’s app). With ancestors and descendants, a descendant’s other parent is drawn too, without its own parents, so every offspring appears with both parents; in the sample pedigree 344 of the 375 animals have such a parent. The focal animals are typed, or an animal is clicked in the drawing (a repeated animal’s symbol counts as the animal); the clicked animal becomes the only focal animal, as in nprcgenekeepr’s Pedigree Browser. With more than 1,000 animals chosen, the app asks before drawing them (about 9 seconds for 1,000 animals and 50 for 2,000 on the computer measured). A sire or dam with no row of its own is added with addParents() and named, so such a file is drawn; the Checks tab still lists it. The Animals tab shows the animals chosen.
  • New: runPedigreeApp()’s app chooses what it draws: up to four conditions from the file’s columns (those whose names begin with “affected”, in any case, chosen at first), each labelled “Affected (its name)”, and a column of numbers cut at a cut-off the legend states, such as “Affected (glucose >= 126)”; the marks makePedigreeMatingLayout() draws, found by their names in any case and by Pedixplorer’s avail and deceased, and listed on the page; lines at right angles or straight; and a twins file (id1, id2, code; MZ twin, DZ twin and UZ twin, or kinship2’s 1, 2 and 3), checked with checkTwinRelations(), a pair drawn when both its animals are. A file’s yes-or-no values are read as TRUE, T, yes, Y or 1 and FALSE, F, no, N or 0, in any case; before, a condition written 1 and 0 was drawn as unknown for every animal, with no message, and a mark written so stopped the drawing. A column with any other value is left out and named. The sample pedigree opens with its file of 3 twin pairs.
  • New: runPedigreeApp()’s app saves what it shows. On the Diagram tab, the SVG, PDF and PNG buttons save the drawing through savePedigreeDiagram(), at that function’s own page (10 inches wide); on the Animals tab, a button saves the animals chosen as a CSV file with every column of the file, which the app opens again to the same drawing. The pictures need the chromote package and Google Chrome or Chromium; without them the picture buttons are greyed and the page says what is missing, and the CSV button still works.
  • New: makePedigreeMatingLayout() draws a pedigree with a sire or dam that has no row of its own, without that parent: an animal whose other parent is unknown is drawn with no line up, as a founder is. It stopped with R’s own messages on many such pedigrees (676 of 1,181 random ones), as nprcgenekeepr’s still does; addParents() adds the missing rows. It also stops on an id on more than one row, naming it, where it stopped with “node stack overflow”.

Kinship and relatedness

  • kinship() computes the kinship matrix, dense or sparse; identical twins get the kinship of an animal with itself.
  • New: kinship()’s parent arguments are sire and dam, in the places of nprcgenekeepr’s fatherId and motherId, and it stops when a known sire’s or dam’s generation number (pdepth) is not below its offspring’s, naming the animal. Before, kinship2’s call form kinship(id, dadid, momid, sex) gave a wrong matrix with no error, taking the sex codes for generation numbers. makePedigreeMatingLayout(), unless given a kinshipMatrix, passes the pedigree’s gen column to kinship(), so it stops the same way. The help page and the README name the functions kinship2 and Pedixplorer also export.
  • New: ibdMatrix() builds an IBD matrix from pairs of ids and their values, and findUnrelated() finds a set of unrelated genotyped animals.

Pedigree structure

  • findGeneration(), findPedigreeNumber(), getParents(), getOffspring(), getFounders(), isFounder(), hasBothParents() and getIdsWithOneParent().
  • New: the pedigree argument is ped in getParents(), getOffspring() and getIdsWithOneParent(), in the place of nprcgenekeepr’s pedSourceDf and uPed, and addBackSecondParents(trimmedPed, ped) calls the trimmed pedigree trimmedPed, in the place of uPed. A call that passes the pedigree by position is unchanged; one that names the old argument stops with “unused argument”.
  • New: the pedigree is the first argument in getProbandPedigree(ped, probands), getDescendantPedigree(ped, probands), trimPedigree(ped, probands, ...) and hasBothParents(ped, id), as in the other functions that take one; nprcgenekeepr takes the ids first. A call that names both arguments is unchanged; one that passes them in nprcgenekeepr’s order stops with “$ operator is invalid for atomic vectors”.
  • New: familyCheck() checks family ids against the family trees the sires and dams form.
  • New: countOffspring() counts each animal’s offspring (the animals naming it as sire or dam, each once), and getMatings() lists each sire and dam with an offspring recorded with both, once, with the number of offspring they share: the matings a drawing draws.
  • New: findGeneration(alignMates = TRUE) puts, where it can be done, the sire and dam of each offspring in the same generation, as kinship2’s kindepth(align = TRUE) does; its help lists the steps. On the pedigrees its tests compare it equals kinship2’s on most, and unlike kinship2’s its answer does not depend on the order of the rows. The default is unchanged.
  • New: getMatings(matings = ) lists declared matings too. Given the table makePedigreeMatingLayout(matings = ) takes, it adds each pair declared mated with no offspring together after the matings built from offspring, in the table’s order, with offspring 0, so its rows are the matings the drawing draws, in its order. In both functions a row naming a pair that has offspring together is set aside without a message, so getMatings()’s result can be passed back; before, the layout said it left out such a row when one of the pair had no row of its own, and stopped on an animal recorded as both sire and dam of one offspring. Without matings, the result is as before.

Checking and repair

  • checkTwinRelations(), addParents(), addBackSecondParents() and correctParentSex().
  • New: checkPedigree() lists each problem in a pedigree, one row per problem, and changes nothing.
  • New: recodePedigree() rewrites other ways of writing an unknown parent and a sex into pedkindraw’s codes. By default a parent written "0" or "NA", or left empty, becomes NA, unless it is the id of a row. A sex written as a word ("male", "female", "hermaphrodite", "unknown") or its first letter, in any case, becomes "M", "F", "H" or "U", as do the numbers 1 and 2 (male and female) and 3 and 4 (unknown); a sex it does not know is left for checkPedigree() to report. kinship2’s sample.ped and testped1, which write an unknown parent as 0 and sex as 1 and 2, then give kinship2’s own kinship.

Trimming and shrinking

  • trimPedigree(), getProbandPedigree(), getDescendantPedigree(), removeUnknownAnimals(), removeUninformativeFounders() and shrinkPedigree().
  • New: the steps of shrinkPedigree(), exported under kinship2’s names: bitSize(), findUnavailable(), findAvailNonInform() and findAvailAffected().
  • New: shrinkPedigree(), findAvailNonInform() and findAvailAffected() stop in the same way when affected, the argument or the column, holds a number other than 0 and 1, which they counted as affected; bitSize() and findUnavailable(), which do not use the status, do not read the column.
  • New: removeAnimals() removes the listed animals and sets to NA each sire or dam entry that names one of them, so no animal is left with a parent that has no row; an offspring keeps its other parent. kinship2’s pedigree.trim() stops when an offspring would keep only one parent, and Pedixplorer’s subset(del_parents = "one") clears that parent too.
  • New: getNearRelativePedigree(ped, probands, maxDist) keeps the animals within a distance of the probands, read from kinship (1 the proband, 2 a parent, offspring or full sibling, 3 a grandparent, half sibling, uncle or aunt, 4 a first cousin), and each parent that joins their families, as Pedixplorer’s useful_inds(max_dist = ) does; a parent left out becomes NA in its offspring’s row.
  • New: ?shrinkPedigree’s example draws the whole pedigree with the animals shrinking removed filled, from idTrimmed, as a condition column (affected_removed, which the legend calls “Affected (removed)”). kinship2’s plot.pedigree.shrink() draws only the animals kept.

Converters

  • New: asPedFrame() converts a kinship2 pedigree or pedigreeList and a Pedixplorer Pedigree to pedkindraw’s pedigree, twins table and layout hints. kinship2 and Pedixplorer are suggested, never required.
  • New: asPedFrame() returns a fourth element, matings: the pairs a kinship2 object’s relation code 4 or a Pedixplorer object’s “Spouse” rows declare mated, as the data frame of sire and dam that makePedigreeMatingLayout(matings = ) and getMatings(matings = ) take, or NULL when the object has none. Each row is kept as the object holds it, a pair with offspring together or named twice included; the male is the sire, else the female is the dam, else the two are in the object’s order. A mate hint row naming such a pair is kept. Draw with makePedigreeMatingLayout(x$ped, hints = x$hints, matings = x$matings). Before, spouse pairs were left out, and so were mate hint rows naming them, with a message.

Documentation

  • New: vignette("speed", package = "pedkindraw"), “Speed and size limits”, gives the seconds each of pedkindraw’s functions took on one machine, by the number of animals from 300 to 100,000, beside the kinship2 and Pedixplorer functions that do the same; where each one stopped and its memory there; and how large a drawing can be drawn and read. A script in the repository, tools/checkSpeedTables.R, checks every number on the page against the timing records in tools/timing/results/. drawPedigreeDiagram()’s help gives the measured size of a drawing and points to the page, as do ?pedkindraw and the other two vignettes.
